CapabilityValue.description:
What a Provider declares it can do for a key (spec 05 `ProviderInstance`).

Rule: SB-6.

local.description: Node-local ordinal, allocated by the owning registry.

node.description: Owning node; `0`, the local node, throughout v4.0 (X7).

DataContractId.description:
A namespaced contract id matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$`,
for example `ezsdr.stream.cf32`.

Rule: SB-1, SC-2.

Driving.description: Whether the coordinator steps this instance (MA-15, MA-30).

stepped.description:
True for a model the coordinator drives; a hardware Provider never receives
a `step` (MA-15).

Duration.description:
An elapsed time: integer ticks in a named clock domain (TM-1, TM-4 decision T4).

The domain tag is what stops 1 000 ticks at 20 Msps being added to a 200 MHz
point as a silent factor-of-ten error.

EnvelopeFidelity.description:
The value set MA-42 gives timing and continuity: `none < envelope <
hardware_quirk < real`. `real` is added to Vision §14's sets, which stop at
`hardware_quirk` and leave a Hardware Run with nothing to record although the
same section says every Run records the vector.

Rule: MA-42.

oneOf.description: Not modelled at all; an `ideal` Mock profile declares this (Vision §13).
A specific hardware quirk is emulated.

Fidelity.description:
What a Run's models actually claim, per aspect. A Run's value per aspect is the
**weakest** over its bound Providers, so a Hardware Run with a best-effort
MockPeripheral records `timing: envelope`.

Rule: MA-42, RS-41. Vision §14.

continuity.description: How faithfully continuity and gaps are modelled.

rf.description: How faithfully the RF path is modelled.

Ident.description:
A name inside one document, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.

Names are compared as bytes; there is no case folding and no Unicode
normalisation, so the canonical form of OV-15 stays byte-comparable.

Rule: SB-1.

ModuleId.description:
Names a Module implementation in the registry, matching
`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*$`, at most 256 bytes.

The reverse-DNS-ish namespaced form (`ezsdr.test.provider`) is what keeps two
vendors' Modules from colliding; the Kernel checks the shape, not the authority.

Rule: SB-1, MA-31.

ModuleRef.description: A Module by id and version (MA-31).

Namespace.description:
A dotted sequence of `Ident`s owned by a Vocabulary or a Module,
matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$`.

Rule: SB-1.

NodeId.description:
A node in the (future) multi-host deployment. `0` (the local node) is the only legal value in v4.0.

Rule: X7 (`00-overview.md`); it qualifies every id of TM-11, SC-6, SB-3 and MA-38.

Port.description:
A name, a direction and a contract id, and nothing more. Per-port parameters
the Kernel does not interpret — a tensor shape, a maximum PDU length — live in
the `ComponentDescriptor`'s parameters (MA-36), not here.

Rule: SC-1.

direction.description: Whether the component consumes or produces here (SC-1).

name.description: Port name, unique within its component (MA-37); an `Ident` (SB-1, SC-1).

PortDirection.description: Which way samples flow through a `Port` (SC-1).

ProfileRef.description:
A declared profile, by name and version. Vision §59 bumps a Mock profile's
version on measurement.

Rule: SB-22, MA-33 (decision B7).

Resource.description:
One node of a Provider's composite resource tree: a device with channels,
streams, a timekeeper, GPIO banks and sensors beneath it, each with its own
`ResourceId` and its own declared capabilities.

Rule: MA-10, SB-33.

capabilities.description: What it declares it can do (SB-6).

id.description: This node's address in the tree (SB-3).

kind.description: What kind of node it is; a Spec resource's `kind` must match (SB-34).

ports.description:
The Ports this node carries, for a node that is a stream endpoint. A Spec
links a component to a bound resource through one of these, which is how
Vision §7's `PHY Processor -> SampleStream -> Radio Port` is expressible;
without them `PortRef.component` could name a resource but no contract
could be checked against it (MA-10, SB-15, SC-1, SC-3).

shareable.description:
Whether more than one Spec resource may bind to this node. Default `false`:
a channel or a stream is exclusive, while Vision §8's GPIO banks "may share
the timekeeper" of §39, so which is which is the Provider's declaration and
never the Kernel's knowledge (MA-10, SB-34, OV-21).

ResourceId.description:
Names a resource, or a sub-resource, inside the composite tree a Provider declares.

The path is a non-empty sequence of segments matching
`^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+){0,15}$`, at most 256 bytes; `dev0/rx/0` names
channel 0 of the receive sub-tree of `dev0`. Vision §49 asks only for the node qualification; the
path replaces §49's flat `local` because a channel or a timekeeper must be
addressable (`00-overview.md` "Where these specs depart from the Vision").

Rule: SB-1, SB-3, SB-33, SB-34 (`03-spec-and-binding.md`), X7.

node.description: Owning node; `0`, the local node, throughout v4.0 (X7).

path.description: Slash-joined path through the composite resource tree (SB-34).

anyOf.description: A signed 64-bit integer, written as an exact decimal by the canonicaliser (OV-15).

A finite float; a non-finite one is refused rather than written as `null`,
because a `Value` reaches the sealed Manifest through `prepare.effective`,
the coercion records and the action log (OV-15, X9).
A list of scalars; nesting deeper is refused (SB-4).
A map of scalars; nesting deeper is refused (SB-4).

Value.description:
A scalar, or a list or map of scalars nested at most one level.

A Spec is data, not a document tree: one level is what a structured parameter
such as a capture request needs, and more invites the schema-inside-a-schema
that Vision §9 rejects.

Rule: SB-4.

arm_after.description:
Instances that must be armed before this one, which is how the device that
sources PPS is armed first (SB-39).

driving.description: Whether the coordinator steps it (MA-15, MA-30).

min_command_lead.description:
The least lead this instance needs between receiving a timed Action and that
Action's instant, in `host.monotonic`; absent means zero. The only envelope
value the Kernel reads (MA-10, RS-19, KA-7).

module.description: Which Module and version supplies it (MA-31).

profile.description: The declared profile, when it has one (SB-22, Vision §33).
